deck_title: Arbor Basin: how the system is operated

bullets: Structure, operating policy, and one year of simulated results
slides.notes: Counts and run horizon are read from the model header.

slides.title: What this deck covers
bullets: The physical system: two basins joined by one transbasin diversion
The operating policy: nine rule groups, west basin to east basin
The decision levers an external workflow can move

slides.title: West basin: a five-reservoir cascade
bullets: Aspen through Elm, four of them power reservoirs. The Transbasin Diversion at Cedar is the only water leaving this basin.
slides.notes: Dashed edges are data and head links, not water: Aspen's tailwater is linked to Birch's pool elevation, and Dogwood's to Elm's. Drawn as a subset of the 41-object network; the whole model on one slide is not readable when projected.

slides.title: East basin: Hickory and the irrigation complex
bullets: The transbasin water arrives above Hickory, which supplies Juniper, the interstate minimum flow, and the Linden and Mulberry canals.
slides.notes: Aggregate sites are drawn as single nodes; their districts are separate objects in the model. The two groundwater objects exchange water laterally and are recharged by canal seepage and irrigation returns.

slides.title: The six reservoirs the policy operates
bullets: Every rule group below is named for one of these reservoirs.

slides.title: West basin, upper cascade: operate, then protect

annotations.Aspen Rules: Draws the pool toward the monthly guide curve, then overrides that if a limit is crossed.
annotations.Aspen Rules/Cause Sporadic Error: A deliberate tripwire: aborts the run when Cedar's Diversion Min Elevation is out of range.
annotations.Aspen Rules/Aspen Operate to Guide Curve: The base operation: release to move the pool toward the Elevation Guide Curve.
annotations.Aspen Rules/Aspen Outflow Min: Floors the release at the minimum outflow.
annotations.Aspen Rules/Aspen Elevation Min: Cuts the release when the pool would fall below its minimum.
annotations.Aspen Rules/Aspen Elevation Max: Increases the release when the pool would exceed its maximum.
annotations.Birch Rules: The same pattern one reservoir down, with an outflow target as the base operation.
annotations.Birch Rules/Birch Outflow Target: The base operation: release to the target outflow.
annotations.Birch Rules/Birch Outflow Min: Floors the release at the minimum outflow.
annotations.Birch Rules/Birch Elevation Min: Cuts the release when the pool would fall below its minimum.
annotations.Birch Rules/Birch Elevation Max: Increases the release when the pool would exceed its maximum.

slides.notes: Agenda order is ASCENDING, so within a group the rule listed last fires first and the elevation limits, listed first, take final priority.

slides.title: The hinge: what the west basin can spare

annotations.Transbasin Diversion: Decides how much water leaves the west basin for the east.
annotations.Transbasin Diversion/Cedar Available for: Offers the storage above Cedar's Diversion Min Elevation, plus inflow, less the required minimum outflow.
annotations.Cedar Rules: Operates the west basin's storage workhorse to its monthly guide curve.
annotations.Cedar Rules/Cedar End of Month Guide Cur: Solves for guide-curve storage on the last day of the month, and walks toward it on other days.
annotations.Cedar Rules/Cedar Outflow Min: Floors the release at the minimum outflow.
annotations.Cedar Rules/Cedar Elevation Min: Applies the minimum from the Pool Elevation Limits table.
annotations.Cedar Rules/Cedar Elevation Max: Applies the maximum from the Pool Elevation Limits table.
annotations.Dogwood Irrigation: Computes west-basin irrigation availability the same way, gated by Dogwood's own floor.
annotations.Dogwood Irrigation/Dogwood Available for: Offers the storage above Dogwood's Diversion Min Elevation to its irrigation diversion.

slides.notes: Cedar.Diversion Min Elevation and Cedar.Pool Elevation Limits are scalar slots written before a run by the input DMIs.

slides.title: East basin: senior rights come first

annotations.Hickory Rules: The east basin's water-rights logic. The firing order is the policy.
annotations.Hickory Rules/Interstate Flow Requiremen: Reserves the interstate minimum first, by setting the Juniper Diversion's minimum bypass.
annotations.Hickory Rules/Hickory Pass Natural Flows: Passes the natural flow arriving above the reservoir, up to what Juniper and the interstate minimum need.
annotations.Hickory Rules/Supplement Juniper from Hi: Releases stored water for Juniper, but only while the pool is above its supplement threshold.
annotations.Hickory Rules/Reduce Hickory Diversion: Cuts the canal supply to Linden and Mulberry in favour of Juniper's senior rights.
annotations.Hickory Rules/Hickory Elevation Min Redu: Cuts the diversion further when the pool is below its minimum.
annotations.Hickory Rules/Hickory Elevation Min: Cuts the release when the pool would fall below its minimum.
annotations.Hickory Rules/Hickory Elevation Max: Increases the release when the pool would exceed its maximum.

slides.notes: Hickory.Pool Elevation Min to Supplement Irrigation is the scalar threshold in the supplement rule, and is DMI-written.

slides.title: Lower cascade: the same two safeguards

annotations.Dogwood Rules: The safeguard pattern only: floors and ceilings, no separate base operation.
annotations.Dogwood Rules/Dogwood Outflow Min: Floors the release at the minimum outflow.
annotations.Dogwood Rules/Dogwood Elevation Min: Cuts the release when the pool would fall below its minimum.
annotations.Dogwood Rules/Dogwood Elevation Max: Increases the release when the pool would exceed its maximum.
annotations.Elm Rules: The bottom reservoir of the cascade, with a pool elevation target and a flood release rule.
annotations.Elm Rules/Elm Pool Elevation Target: The base operation: release toward the target pool elevation.
annotations.Elm Rules/Elm Required Spill: Makes the flood release when one is required.
annotations.Elm Rules/Elm Outflow Min: Floors the release at the minimum outflow.
annotations.Elm Rules/Elm Elevation Min: Cuts the release when the pool would fall below its minimum.
annotations.Elm Rules/Elm Elevation Max: Increases the release when the pool would exceed its maximum.

slides.notes: Both groups call the three shared functions in the set's utility group: OutflowForMinOutflowRules, OutflowForMinElevationRules, OutflowForMaxElevationRules.

slides.title: Post-processing: what the run reports

annotations.Post-processing: Fires last, and writes the system-wide summary slots nothing else reads.
annotations.Post-processing/Interstate Flow Requirem: Records any shortfall below the interstate minimum flow.
annotations.Post-processing/System Energy: Sums energy across the power objects into System Data.
annotations.Post-processing/System Spill: Sums spill volume across the reservoirs.
annotations.Post-processing/System Depletion Shortag: Sums depletion shortage across the water users.
annotations.Post-processing/Energy Cumulative: Accumulates each power object's energy over the run.

slides.notes: These write the System Data slots the output DMIs export after a run: Total Energy, the west- and east-basin irrigation totals, Total Spill Volume, Total Transbasin Diversion, and Total Depletion Shortage.

slides.title: The levers an external workflow moves
bullets: Cedar.Diversion Min Elevation - the floor below which the transbasin diversion is cut off
Cedar.Pool Elevation Limits - the adjustable maximum and minimum operating elevations
Dogwood.Diversion Min Elevation - the floor for west-basin irrigation access
Hickory.Pool Elevation Min to Supplement Irrigation - how deeply east-basin storage is drawn for irrigation
Input DMIs write these before a run; output DMIs export the System Data totals after it.
slides.notes: All four are scalar slots on the objects named. The DMIs are listed in the model's DMI catalog: ArborInputDMI, ArborMRMInputs, From Borg-RiverWare, and their output counterparts.

slides.title: Simulated pool elevations, 2018
bullets: One reservoir from each part of the story: the two power reservoirs at the top, Cedar at the hinge, and Hickory in the east.
slides.notes: All four are in metres, so the four traces share one value axis. The elevation ranges differ by more than 100 m, which is why the lower reservoirs look flat.

slides.title: What actually crossed the divide
bullets: Cedar's release, the transbasin diversion it feeds, and what Hickory passed downstream.
slides.notes: All three are flows in cms. The transbasin series is the outflow of the Transbasin Diversion object, which enters the east basin above Hickory.

bullets: Arbor Basin is the CADSWES training model, not an operating model of a real basin.
